basis: Infantile lysosomal storage with defining severe neurodevelopmental disease and skeletal dysplasia; common hepatic or renal functional damage is not established.

decisions.hepatic: none: hepatomegaly alone does not establish function-impairing storage; conjugated hyperbilirubinemia has no stated frequency
decisions.renal: none: nephrotic syndrome is reported, but its frequency is unspecified and involvement in at least 30% is uncertain
decisions.neurologic: primary: severe developmental impairment and progressive CNS disease characterize the infantile phenotype
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal dysplasia is supported by the explicit skeletal-involvement parent and characteristic skeletal abnormalities

basis: Defining microphthalmia, pulmonary hypoplasia (4/5) and diaphragm defect (6/6); major neurologic impairment includes ID (1/1). Malrotation (2/7) is below 30%.

decisions.neurologic: involved: severe neurodevelopmental impairment is a major clinical feature; intellectual disability was present in 1/1 assessed patient
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: congenital diaphragm skeletal-muscle defect is part of the defining triad and occurred in 6/6 patients

basis: GAG storage with defining skeletal disease; valvular disease and airway obstruction each affect >50% over the course. Common hearing loss and nerve entrapment omitted at cap.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal disease and short stature are defining features of attenuated MPS II, supported by its skeletal-storage ancestry

basis: Neurogenic neoplasm of the eyelid establishes ocular location and neural tissue of origin; no additional organ damage is established.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurogenic denotes neural tissue of origin, supporting the peripheral-nerve axis alongside the eyelid location

basis: Congenital renal collecting-duct ectasia; distal renal tubular acidosis is separately diagnosed despite its 30-79% annotation. Urinary infections are separate complications.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: distal renal tubular acidosis is a separately diagnosed associated disorder; hypercalciuria alone does not establish additional endocrine or metabolic damage

basis: Intellectual disability and marfanoid skeletal disease define the syndrome; atrial septal defect is annotated at 30-79%. Dental crowding and high palate alone do not establish functional damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dental crowding (5/6) and high palate (5/5) establish morphology, without demonstrated dental loss, oral dysfunction or tissue damage

basis: Inherited glycosylation disorder whose recognized subtypes are defined by intellectual disability or developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurodevelopmental dysfunction defines both recognized subtypes and therefore the usual phenotype across this umbrella

basis: Bladder and intestinal dysfunction define MMIHS2. Pulmonary and cardiovascular findings each have singleton assessments; these do not establish prevalence of at least 30%.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: aneurysm, PDA and elevated pulmonary pressure each have 1/1 annotations; selected singleton observations do not establish common involvement across the syndrome
decisions.pulmonary: none: hypoplasia and bronchomalacia each have 1/1 annotations; these singleton observations do not establish involvement in at least 30% of patients

basis: Defective inflammatory-mediator regulation causes defining angioedema and chronic urticaria. Common intrinsic airway disease is not established.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: chronic urticaria and cutaneous angioedema constitute the defining skin disease phenotype, rather than an incidental passing rash

basis: Heart and ectodermal skin/dental defects define disease; developmental impairment is reported in ~33-50%. Scoliosis (1/3) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: dental ectodermal dysplasia is part of the defining phenotype, including microdontia and premature tooth loss (each 1/3); teeth belong to this axis
